display.purpose: Module-opening section titles (e.g. 'Detect who's ready to buy, right now.'). One per screen region.

kpi.purpose: ICP scores, pipeline counts, stage KPIs. The numbers the operator reads at a glance. Never used for non-numeric content.

body.purpose: AI output text, prospect notes, descriptions, drawer content. Minimum weight 400 for decision-critical text.

ui.purpose: Card titles, button labels, tab labels, input values. The workhorse of the interface.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows, badge text, kanban column headers, score-kpi-label. Uppercase. Max 3-word phrases.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: k-cards and interactive rows on hover. Always paired with translateY(-1px).

shadows.name: cta-lift
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover. The strongest interactive shadow.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Right-side slide panel. Communicates this layer floats above the kanban.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Full overlays (call prep, add prospect). The one case where near-black shadow is used — modal scale requires structural contrast.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions: drawer open/close, tab switch, hover lift.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color-only transitions: button hover background, border-color on focus.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Most interactive element transitions (hover lift, opacity, background).

motion.name: score-bar-reveal
motion.purpose: ICP score bar fill animation on results load.

narrative.overview:
Corridor's visual world is a command center for commercial intelligence. The interface receives signals in real-time, sorts them by urgency, and routes the operator toward action. Every module is a workstation — Scanner, Pipeline, Send Queue, CMO IA — and the visual system communicates that each one has a job to do. The tone is operational: dense but not cluttered, authoritative but not cold.

The palette runs on a single systemic logic: System Blue (#1a2b5e) holds authority, Signal Sky (#93A8D4) marks connection and interface scaffolding, and the semantic signal colors (green, amber, red) carry real operational meaning. They appear only when a prospect is moving, an alert fires, or a deadline is overdue — never decoratively.

The dual landing / app typography split is intentional. The public-facing landing (Geist) speaks as a product platform. The private app (Fraunces + Plus Jakarta Sans) speaks as an instrument. These worlds do not mix.
keyCharacteristics: Signal-driven hierarchy: color carries urgency, not decoration
Fraunces reserved strictly for KPIs and section titles
Navy-tinted shadows throughout — no pure black anywhere
Operational density: 6-column kanban, tabbed modules, compact cards
Semantic color vocabulary with named states (signal-green, signal-amber, signal-red)

rules.name: The No Pure Black Rule
rules.body: No #000000, no rgba(0,0,0,...) anywhere. Shadows, overlays, and dark text all use navy-tinted values: rgba(26,43,94,...) for shadows, #1e2a45 for text.

rules.name: The Signal Color Contract
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only when they carry the meaning their name implies. Using any of the three decoratively breaks the semantic contract and trains users to ignore real alerts.

rules.name: The Fraunces Gate
rules.body: Fraunces appears only in KPI values and section titles. Any heading that is a label, card title, button, badge, or nav item uses Plus Jakarta Sans.

rules.name: The Weight 300 Warning
rules.body: font-weight:300 at 13px or smaller is fragile on non-Retina screens. Limit it to decorative sub-copy. AI output and any decision-critical text must be weight 400 or heavier.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface starts flat. A shadow is a response to state (hover, open, active), not a design choice.

rules.name: The Nav Glass Rule
rules.body: The navigation bar is the only element with backdrop-filter: blur(). Do not apply it elsewhere.

rules.name: The Pill Boundary
rules.body: Border-radius 20px (pill) is exclusively for status chips: badges, signal tags, count bubbles. Buttons, cards, and inputs are never pill-shaped.

rules.name: The Uniform Radius Warning
rules.body: Avoid giving every component the same radius. The graduated vocabulary — 2/6/8/10/12/14/20 — communicates surface hierarchy.

dos: Do tint every shadow with the navy channel: rgba(26,43,94,...). Even modal overlays should prefer navy-tinted shadows over pure black.
Do use Fraunces exclusively for KPI values and module-opening section titles.
Do use transform: translateY(-1px) and shadow together on interactive elements — always as a pair.
Do use font-weight 400 or higher for any text the user reads to make a decision.
Do use cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) at 0.2–0.3s for all panel transitions.
Do add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any numeric column that updates dynamically.
donts: Don't use signal colors (green, amber, red) decoratively — semantic use only.
Don't apply border-radius: 20px to buttons, cards, or input fields.
Don't use font-weight: 300 for AI output body text or decision-critical content.
Don't add a shadow to a card at rest — borders define cards, shadows respond to state.
Don't apply backdrop-filter: blur() outside the fixed nav bar.
Don't introduce a third font family into the app (Fraunces + Plus Jakarta Sans only).
Don't use pure #000000 or rgba(0,0,0,1) as text color — use Ink (#1e2a45).
